text:
Your body in what joy of fluttering,

what nearness of trills, oh agitated

passion of you, inspired turtledove,

of blue and feather in clear blue! (Uccello)


Bird. Go out. Write on the ground

the joy of your enamored cage.

Let the sword of a hawk

brandished for the duel be a smiling perch.


I, your parted foliage. Permanent

tree where your destiny resounds,

will read your trajectory. One guesses


so well what is awaited... Of the oblique

path, what do you care, oh different

blackbird of light, if you come to the holm oak!

translation.title: Birds for Yvonne
translation.editorial_note: The translation preserves the bird imagery, Uccello aside, and the beloved's flight toward the tree.
